title: Replay new refusal rules over last 50 requests before landing
summary: Add a replay step: when a candidate adds or changes a refusal rule, run the rule over the last 50 recorded requests and accepted readings, record the refused count and list, hold the candidate if over 10% unless its criteria intend a higher rate, and include the replay summary in the verifier brief within its size limit.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added; cargo test, clippy -D warnings, fmt required.
Criteria run tests showing counts, lists and holds.
The hold is enforced in code, not prose.
Verifier sees the replay summary in its brief.
Limited to the four named files.
Empty history is reported as no replay, not a pass.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: prevent a new refusal rule (reading rule, admission rule, dispatch hold) from landing untried; audience is Athena's operator and the verifier.
Recorded requests and accepted readings are supplied to the replay as input (loaded by the run code); tests use fixtures, since records/ is absent from the copy.
A candidate is detected as changing a refusal rule by a flag/classification on the candidate; the replay applies the rule as a function over a reading.
The 10% threshold is a constant in code; an intended higher rate is declared in the candidate's acceptance criteria and parsed by a simple marker.
Held means the job is held with the refused list, not landed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs using fixture requests and accepted readings shows the replay of a candidate refusal rule reports the count refused and lists which requests; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A test shows a candidate rule refusing more than 10% of the replayed accepted readings is held with the list of refused requests, and that a rule at or under 10% is not held; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A test shows a candidate whose criteria declare a higher refusal rate as intended is not held, though the replay is still recorded; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

The replay window is the last 50 recorded requests (fewer if fewer exist); a test with more than 50 fixtures shows only the latest 50 are used, and an empty history is reported as no replay, not as a pass.

A test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs shows the verifier brief includes the replay summary (refused count, total, refused list) for a candidate changing a refusal rule, omits it otherwise, and stays within the brief size limit even with a long refusal list; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs invokes the replay for a candidate that adds or changes a refusal rule and records the result; a test or Grep of the diff shows the hold path is wired into the run pipeline.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the refusal-rule replay, the 10% hold and the verifier brief summary.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) is changed; the 10% threshold is a code constant.

out_of_scope: Changing any existing refusal rule's behavior
departures: Hard job touching the run pipeline, verifier brief and a hold gate across three crates; costs and failure risk above reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed and rejected attempts and stopped drains caused by an untried refusal rule that refused its own fix three times.
hard_reason: Adds a gate that holds candidates, and changes the run pipeline and the verifier brief that judges other jobs.
